title: wt cleanup --json
description: The one document `wt cleanup --json` prints, on success and on failure. `rows` is always present. A row's `evidence` is ABSENT when no proof was found (never null, never "unknown"); `unknown: true` is the separate flag for "could not be determined". `base` is absent when no default branch was found; `base.fetched_at` is absent when no fetch ran or the fetch failed (it is written only after a fetch that worked). `notes` is absent when empty; otherwise it holds the caveats the text view prints under its header (a lowered `--min-age`, model-artifact protection off because the registry failed to load, no registry), and a consumer that acts on `rows` must read it: with protection off a row holding a registered `local_path` artifact carries no `protected_artifact` blocker. `fetch` is absent when no fetch ran ("not attempted", including a repository with no remote at all); when present, `ok` and `error` are about origin (the base is origin's), and `remotes`, present when the repository has more than one remote or a remote other than origin, lists every remote considered with its own `ok`/`error`, or `skipped: true` for a non-origin remote excluded by `remote.<name>.skipFetchAll` (origin is always fetched); a repository with remotes but no origin has `fetch.ok` false, `fetch.skipped` "no origin remote" and no `at`, with its other remotes' results in `remotes`; each remote is fetched by its own `git fetch --prune <remote>`. A row's `age_days` is absent when the age could not be determined (0 means a known age under a day). `evidence` only ever holds a proof, except `rescued`, which is not a merge proof: it means a wt rescue record (a ref under refs/wt/rescued/) holds the commits, so removing the row loses none of those commits (losses the record does not cover, such as ignored files, still apply); `cherry-equivalent` and `patch-id` are reserved in the frozen enum and are never emitted as `evidence` today (weak signals appear as a `weak_signal` reason). On failure `error` is set (a nil error is reported as "unknown error"), `rows` is empty and base/fetch/gh are absent. A row's `hard_stop` is the code of the first blocker that refuses its removal outright (absent when none does; a `held` or `default_branch` blocker needs approval, not a hard stop); rows include the primary checkout, the default branch and held rows, each with its verdict. A local row's `upstream` is the remote-tracking ref folded into it (that ref has no row of its own in a text view; `gone` true means the configured upstream no longer exists, and then `tip`, `status` and `evidence` are absent). Pinned to wt/internal/cleanup/json.go by wt/cmd/wt/cleanup_contract_test.go; a code or enum added there must be added here and in cleanup-list.sample.json in the same change; cleanup-list.fetch-failed.sample.json shows a run whose fetch failed and cleanup-list.no-origin.sample.json a repository with no origin remote.
